text:
Carolina arrives with four straight wins and a 7-0 rout of Winnipeg on Sunday, a game in which Pyotr Kochetkov stopped all 26 shots. The Hurricanes are doing it without Jordan Staal, and Seth Jarvis has moved in beside Martinook and Ehlers while Mark Jankowski (17:02 a night, up from 13:11) and William Carrier (14:14, up from 11:39) pick up extra minutes. Nashville won a shootout over Tampa Bay on Friday after trailing in the third, but it is 2-1-2 in its last five, and Ryan O'Reilly, a point-getter in five straight, is the subject of trade rumors (NHL Trade Rumors posted that he is to be traded).

The numbers favor Carolina. At five on five, the Hurricanes have taken 58% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, against Nashville's 46%. Our model projects 3.53 goals for CAR and 2.60 for NSH. Carolina's power play is also creating more than Nashville's (0.96 expected goals a game to 0.67), though the Hurricanes take four penalties a game. In net, projected starter Kochetkov is +9.7 in goals saved above expected this season, the number of goals he has stopped beyond what an average goalie would on the same shots. Juuse Saros (projected) is +2.5 this year, after -10.2 last season over 59 games.

Our model gives Sebastian Aho a 35% chance to score and Andrei Svechnikov 34%. Logan Stankoven, a 200th-game milestone and a breakout candidate at 30%, said after Saturday's practice-day win, as Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal posted, "We're not satisfied with one. We want to go for more." For Nashville, Steven Stamkos (34%) tops the model, with Filip Forsberg (32%) riding four straight multi-point games.
